title: Network and Compiler Optimizations for Efficient Linear Algebra Kernels in Private Transformer Inference (Invited Paper)
problem: Fully Homomorphic Encryption-based private transformer inference is extremely slow. Mapping standard kernels to constrained FHE instruction set is difficult. Memory-bound FHE operations with ~0.1 ops/byte limit scalability.
motivation: Enable private inference without compromising latency through algorithm and compiler optimizations.
method: Explores linear algebra kernels for FHE transformer inference: benchmarks two methods (packed row vs BSGS), finds BSGS 13.7x faster at scale; applies network-level pruning reducing feed-forward layers 11.46x; extends Orion to support ciphertext-ciphertext GEMM; performs roofline analysis revealing memory-bound bottleneck.
key_novelty: Compiler and network-level optimizations for FHE-based transformer inference with roofline characterization.
contributions: BSGS outperforms packed row method by 13.7x for transformer-scale linear transformations
Network pruning strategies reducing FHE runtimes by 11.46x
Ciphertext-ciphertext matrix-matrix products and roofline analysis of FHE primitives

metrics.other: roofline shows 0.1 int ops/byte for FHE primitives

limitations: Focuses on linear algebra kernels; full end-to-end system performance not comprehensively evaluated.
primary_theme: compiler optimizations for private transformer inference
